content: LIM2, also known as Lens Fiber Membrane Intrinsic Protein, is a protein encoded by the LIM2 gene in humans. Within the mammalian lens fiber cell membrane, there are five major proteins, with molecular weights ranging from 70 kDa to 19 kDa. The precise biological functions of these proteins remain unclear. One of these proteins, crystalline-gamma-1 (CRYG1; MIM 123660), has a molecular weight of approximately 5 kDa. This protein is characterized by the presence of four transmembrane domains. It serves as a substrate for both cAMP-dependent protein kinase and protein kinase C. Additionally, it has the ability to bind to calmodulin, a calcium-binding messenger protein. These findings collectively suggest that MP19, another name for this protein, may play a role as a junctional component, potentially facilitating communication between lens cells. Furthermore, it has been implicated in the process of cataractogenesis, indicating its involvement in the development of cataracts.
